paragraphs.title: Planning Oppression and Judgment on the Powerful

easy.explanation: Micah says they devise iniquity and work evil upon their beds.
easy.q: What do the wicked devise upon their beds?

easy.explanation: They covet fields and houses and take them by violence.
easy.q: What do they covet and take by violence?

easy.explanation: The LORD says He will devise an evil against the oppressive family.
easy.q: What does the LORD devise against this family?

answers: They plan evil and oppress others
medium.explanation: Their judgment is caused by their planned injustice, greed, and oppression.
medium.q: Why does judgment come upon these powerful people?

medium.explanation: Heritage refers to an inherited possession, especially land or property.
medium.q: In the phrase “a man and his heritage,” what does “heritage” mean?

answers: The loss and division of the people's land
medium.explanation: The lament describes the removal and division of the people's portion and fields.
medium.q: What does the lamentation describe in that day?

answers: Those who seized fields will lose their own portion
Those who stole will receive more land
Those who planned evil will escape unchanged
challenge.explanation: The judgment reverses their actions: those who dispossessed others will lose their own inheritance.
challenge.q: How does the punishment correspond to the oppressors' actions?

answers: They quickly carry out what they planned
They abandon their plans at dawn
challenge.explanation: They plan evil at night and put it into practice as soon as morning comes.
challenge.q: What does “when the morning is light, they practise it” show?

answers: An equal division of all property
challenge.explanation: The people will take up a parable and lament because their portion and fields have been taken away.
challenge.q: What public result of the judgment is described?

paragraphs.title: Rejecting the Prophet and Clarifying God's Judgment

easy.explanation: They tell the prophets not to prophesy.
easy.q: What do the people tell those who prophesy?

easy.explanation: The verse says God's words do good to him that walks uprightly.
easy.q: To whom do God's words do good?

answers: It will not take away their shame
easy.explanation: They reject the prophecy because they do not want words that expose their shame.
easy.q: What do the people imply about the prophet's message?

answers: He says God's words do good to the upright
medium.explanation: The prophet declares that God's words benefit the person who walks uprightly.
medium.q: How does the prophet answer the claim that God's words are harmful or useless?

medium.explanation: Shame means disgrace or dishonor brought upon a person.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “shame” mean?

medium.explanation: The context distinguishes the evil from the upright, showing that judgment addresses the wrongdoers.
medium.q: Who is the warning of judgment directed against?

answers: God's words benefit the upright but are rejected by the wicked
The people prefer war to peace
challenge.explanation: The wicked reject the message, while God's words do good to those who walk uprightly.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the prophet's words?

answers: The people question whether God's judgment is justified
The people ask for more land
The prophet does not know God's will
challenge.explanation: The question challenges the people's attempt to deny or limit the justice of the LORD's actions.
challenge.q: What does the question “Is the spirit of the LORD straitened?” suggest?

answers: God's words do good to those who walk uprightly
There is no judgment at all
The warning applies only to foreigners
challenge.explanation: The passage says God's words benefit the upright, distinguishing them from those under judgment.
challenge.q: Why is the warning not unjust toward everyone?

paragraphs.title: Oppression of Passersby and Expulsion of Women

easy.explanation: They pull off the robe and garment from people passing by securely.
easy.q: What do the oppressors take from people who pass by securely?

easy.explanation: The verse says the women of God's people have been cast out.
easy.q: Whom have they cast out from their pleasant houses?

easy.explanation: The people are told to depart because the land is not their rest.
easy.q: What is said about the people's rest?

answers: Robbing peaceful travelers and expelling women from their homes
medium.explanation: The passage describes the stripping of travelers and the expulsion of women and their children.
medium.q: Which acts of oppression are mentioned together?

answers: A place of peace and security
medium.explanation: Rest refers to a secure and peaceful place where people may dwell.
medium.q: What does “rest” mean in “this is not your rest”?

answers: The land is polluted and will destroy them
There are no houses in the land
medium.explanation: They must leave because the land is polluted and will bring destruction.
medium.q: Why are the people told to depart?

challenge.explanation: The passage shows that the wrongdoing affects women and children as well as property.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between casting out the women and taking glory from the children?

answers: The injustice harms both individuals and families
challenge.explanation: The verses portray oppression against people on the road and families in their homes.
challenge.q: What does the movement from robbing travelers to expelling women reveal?

answers: Pollution and oppression lead to the loss of rest and departure
Rest causes the women to be expelled
Preaching causes the houses to be divided
challenge.explanation: Because the land has been polluted by wrongdoing, it is no longer a place of rest and the people must depart.
challenge.q: Which cause-and-effect summary best fits the passage?

paragraphs.title: Preference for False Prophets and Ambiguous Hope of Gathering Israel

answers: One who speaks of wine and strong drink
easy.explanation: The people accept a prophet who promises to speak of wine and strong drink.
easy.q: What kind of prophet does the people prefer?

answers: Jacob and the remnant of Israel
easy.explanation: The LORD promises to assemble Jacob and gather the remnant of Israel.
easy.q: Whom does the LORD promise to gather?

answers: Their king, with the LORD at their head
easy.explanation: The king passes before them, and the LORD is at their head.
easy.q: Who goes before the people at the end?

answers: His message is comfortable and does not rebuke them
He promises to divide the land
He drives the women from their homes
medium.explanation: They prefer a pleasant, permissive message instead of a warning that confronts their sin.
medium.q: Why do the people prefer the prophet who speaks of wine and strong drink?

medium.explanation: A remnant is what remains after others have been removed or lost.
medium.q: What does “remnant” mean in “the remnant of Israel”?

answers: The people are gathered and pass through the gate under leadership
medium.explanation: The passage describes the people being gathered, breaking through the gate, and going out under their king and the LORD.
medium.q: What picture appears in the closing verses?

answers: It may suggest restoration and growth or gathering under threat
It contains no gathering at all
It concerns only wine and strong drink
challenge.explanation: The imagery can suggest hopeful gathering, but it may also reflect movement caused by danger or judgment.
challenge.q: Why can the hope at the end be described as ambiguous?

answers: Forced departure or guided movement into a new way
Returning only to an abandoned house
challenge.explanation: The movement may represent exile, yet the leadership of the king and the LORD can also suggest guidance into a new path.
challenge.q: What double meaning may be associated with going out through the gate?

answers: A preference for a comfortable message is followed by gathering and leadership
A change from dividing fields to building houses
A change from prayer to warfare only
challenge.explanation: At first the people favor an easy message about drink; at the end the passage presents gathering and leadership under the king and the LORD.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the beginning and the end of this section?
